questions.text: What are the main characteristics of the family system?
questions.text_as_printed: What are the main characteristics of the family system? (A)

answer.value: Family is universal — it is a social system seen in all times and all countries. It is the core of society. It is from the family that neighbourhoods, villages, cities and nations have evolved. Right from their childhood, the members of the family realise their social responsibilities and understand co-operation. The social traditions, morality and behaviour are all controlled by the family. Thus, the family is a universal, permanent and traditional structure.

It fosters social responsibility.
It promotes the care, support, and protection of parents.

questions.text: What is the role of childhood and youth in the social development of an individual?
questions.text_as_printed: What is the role of childhood and youth in the social development of an individual? (A)

answer.value: Childhood and youth occupy an important place in the social development of an individual. The child learns the mother tongue and the fundamental social tenets. Growing up in a family and social environment, the child develops these characteristics and forms friendships with other children of the same age; by mingling with others the child develops leadership qualities and social behaviour, forming healthy social relationships. Later in youth it leads to friendship, independence, security and social acceptance; the behaviour and habits developed in youth continue into adulthood and old age.

questions.text: The joint family system is self-sufficient. - Justify
questions.text_as_printed: The joint family system is self-sufficient. - Justify(D)

answer.value: The joint (undivided) family is self-sufficient: it is mostly self-dependent, encompasses the lives of its members completely and fulfils the majority of their needs. Residence: all members normally live under the same roof. Kitchen: the members usually prepare and consume food in the same kitchen. Religion: all members follow the same religion and worship together. Property: all members own the property and utilise it harmoniously. The oldest member holds the authority to make decisions.

questions.answer_as_printed:
Childhood and Youth in Social Development
A child learns the mother tongue and basic social concepts.
Growing up in a family and social environment, the child adopts corresponding characteristics.
Develops friendships with peers.
Develops leadership qualities by interacting with others.
Social behaviours, demands, and rules influence the child, forming social relationships.
In youth, individuals strive for friendship, freedom, security, and acceptance, and the behaviours and opinions developed during this phase continue into adulthood and old age.

questions.text: What are the characteristics of matriarchal and patriarchal families?
questions.text_as_printed: What are the characteristics of matriarchal and patriarchal families? (A)

answer.value:
Patriarchal Family
The father is the head of the family.
Property transactions are conducted in the father’s name.
Patriarchal families are found in ancient India, China, Egypt, and Rome.
Matriarchal Family
The mother is the head of the family.
Property transactions are conducted in the mother’s name.
Found among the Nair community in Malabar, Kerala, and some tribal communities in north-eastern states.

questions.text: List out the differences between joint family and nuclear family.
questions.text_as_printed: List out the differences between joint family and nuclear family. (A)

answer.value:
Joint Family
Consists of parents, children, grandchildren, and great-grandchildren, spanning more than two generations.
Members live in one house.
Food is prepared in a single kitchen.
Members follow a common religion.
The senior member has decision-making authority.
Nuclear Family
Consists of parents and their unmarried children.
Emphasizes individual freedom.
Includes property rights.
Prevalent due to urbanization and industrialization.
Provides greater freedom to women.
Based on democratic and egalitarian principles.
